chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from one who informed him from him, peace be upon him, who said:
"Pray the two rak'ahs between you and the time when the light is level with your head; and if it is after that, then begin with Fajr."
ai.seo_question: When should the two rak'ahs before Fajr be prayed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential boundary between the pre-dawn voluntary prayer and the obligatory Fajr prayer, using the visual cue of dawn's light reaching head height as the critical marker. In Shia fiqh, this distinction ensures that the two rak'ahs retain their status as distinct voluntary acts if performed early, whereas delaying them past this point integrates them into the Fajr obligation, reflecting the precise temporal definitions of *al-fajr al-sadiq* (true dawn).
